:::{#rem-overfitting-tradeoff}
#### Overfitting and the trade-off

By @thm-epe-decomposition,
$\epe{g_l}{n}{x}$ is the squared bias plus the variance plus $\sigma^2$.
Under a [bias--variance trade-off](#def-bias-variance-tradeoff)
among $g_1, \ldots, g_L$,
moving from $g_l$ to $g_{l+1}$
lowers the expected squared prediction error at $x$
when the squared bias falls by more than the variance rises,
and raises it otherwise.
The smallest of $\epe{g_1}{n}{x}, \ldots, \epe{g_L}{n}{x}$
is often at some $g_l$ with $1 < l < L$
[@james2021islr2e, sec. 2.2.2],
but not always:
if the mean function $\mean$ is a candidate of $g_1$,
the squared bias of $g_1$ can be zero,
and then no later $g_l$ has a smaller squared bias
and, under the trade-off, none has a smaller variance,
so none has a smaller expected squared prediction error.
The procedures past the smallest error
have lowered their squared bias by less than they have raised their variance,
and the rules they produce tend to [overfit](#def-overfitting):
they fit their training sets more closely than the procedure with the smallest error
but predict new observations worse.

:::
